old.reason: Must know computers exist before understanding they follow exact instructions

proposed.reason: Recognising computers as instruction-following devices supports explicit comparison with human instructions; the complete five-device identification/classification claim is not necessary to writing and testing precise everyday algorithms.

changes.counterexampleToWholeNecessity: Learner can independently write/describe an exact sandwich procedure, predict a missing/reordered step and explain that a computer executes literally, without independently recognising at least five embedded-computer devices or sorting all devices.

old.reason: One-to-one correspondence requires knowing the number name sequence

proposed.reason: Matching number names to real objects supports meaningful counting, but rote forward/backward number-sequence production can be learned and assessed without one-to-one object enumeration.

changes.counterexampleToWholeNecessity: Learner independently recites forward0–100/backwards20–0 and continues from arbitrary47, while an object-enumeration task reveals double-counting. The entire rote sequence contract can pass while one-to-one fails.

wholeRoteCounterexample: A learner can produce the complete forward/backward number sequence through 100 from arbitrary starts yet double-count real objects; rote sequence production and one-to-one object enumeration are distinct operations.
preservation: All 1911 intrinsic claims, 1096 teaching-research records, age/context records and source catalogue entries remain byte-identical. The other 4000 dependency records remain structurally identical. No learner state or history changed.
downstreamGate: Requalify eligibility/scheduling and private learner compatibility before staging publication. No reset or automatic source Full promotion.
